caption: The drawing depicts a symmetrical garden design, shown from an overhead perspective. The primary section, central in the composition, is a large, circular parterre with a geometric pattern divided into multiple segments by light tan pathways. The parterre pattern is elaborate, featuring intersecting arcs and pointed oval shapes filled with various clusters of color, including green, yellow, orange, pink, red, and blue, which represent flowerbeds or foliage. The circular garden is bisected by several paths extending outward, forming a cross shape and dividing the surrounding lawn into four roughly triangular sectors. Each of these sectors is colored in shades of green and contains circular tree canopies and individual conical trees depicted in darker green, with tree trunks visible. In the outermost areas beyond the central parterre, groups of trees, bushes, and patches of color suggesting flowering plants are distributed along the edges. The lower right corner contains printed text in blue, identifying the site as “PARTERRE FROM THE JAMES GORDON BENNETT ESTATE THE BLACKWELL SURVEY,” with a small linear scale below. The drawing mainly uses green hues for lawns and trees, light tan for pathways, and a mix of bright colors for the garden beds.
title: J. G. Bennett Estate
